header:
Date: 2026-07-13 15:00 UTC
Duration: 45 minutes
Location: Zoom
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (CTO, IrisAI), Maya Patel (Head of Platform, IrisAI), Leo Santos (SRE, IrisAI), Sam (Product PM, IrisAI)
summary: Intro demo of Redwood Console focusing on per-route usage analytics, mapping billing to product routes, and governance rules for inference routing. Discussed tradeoffs between hosted vs dedicated and private deployment constraints; agreed next steps to run per-route baseline and share pricing + security docs.
topics: Routing policies, fallbacks, and model variants
transcript:
[00:00:00] Alex (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining—uh, quick roll call?
[00:00:08] Jordan (IrisAI, CTO): Jordan here.
[00:00:09] Maya (IrisAI): Maya present.
[00:00:11] Leo (IrisAI): Leo, yep.
[00:00:12] Sam (IrisAI): Sam.
[00:00:14] Priya (Redwood SE): Priya here. Cool, thanks.
[00:00:17] Alex: Great. So, high level goal for today is to show how you can map invoiced spend down to product routes and then attach governance rules so you can keep costs predictable while we preserve latency. We're going to demo the Console — per-route dashboards, cost attribution, and then talk about routing/fallbacks. Sound good?
[00:00:34] Jordan: Yep. We're particularly interested in two things — one is per-feature cost so our product team can understand hot paths, and second is how to set upper bounds or fallbacks when traffic spikes.
[00:00:44] Priya: Perfect. I'll start screen-share and walk through the per-route lenses. Heads up, I might jump between the live Console and a demo spreadsheet we prepared.
[00:00:55] [screen share starts]
[00:01:05] Priya: Ok, on the left here is our Routes view — you can see routes as first-class entities. Notice metric columns: tokens, p99 latency, cost-per-1k tokens, and error rates. For IrisI-sample, I've pre-allocated the route tags you sent so mapping is immediate — looks like 60% of tokens are coming from the question-answering route and that maps to 72% of spend due to long context.
[00:01:33] Maya: That long context is expected — our QA uses full-document lookups. Is there an easy way to attribute cost to product features rather than just endpoints?
[00:01:41] Priya: Yeah, we support hierarchical tags — you can tag an endpoint with feature:qa, team:data, and customer_tier:premium. The Console then lets you pivot. Here in the UI I switch to 'Feature View' and you can see feature:qa shows high token density.
[00:02:00] Alex: And important point — the Console cost model uses tokenized counts and a per-model cost profile. So if you route a request to a larger model variant, the unit cost updates automatically.
[00:02:12] Jordan: Quick question — can we set a routing rule that says: if p95 latency exceeds X or cost per request goes above Y, fallback to a cheaper model automatically?
[00:02:21] Priya: Yes, that's done with routing policies. Example: we have a policy called 'latency-first' that prioritizes lowest p99 model but you can add guardrails like budget caps or error thresholds. It can also cascade: first try dedicated high-perf, then hosted mid, then a quantized variant.
[00:02:36] Leo: When you say "quantized variant" — do you mean 8-bit or int4? We have concerns about quality regressions.
[00:02:44] Priya: Right — we suggest running the Optimize toolkit's quality monitor. You can flag evals for your golden prompt set; Optimize will surface regressions after quantization and suggest acceptable profiles. We usually recommend A/B testing with 10% traffic first.
[00:02:58] [00:03:00] Sam: There's also the question of caching — KV cache? Our embeddings pipeline uses a lot of cache hits.
[00:03:07] Priya: We support prefix and KV caching; Console shows cache hit ratio per route and the effective token reduction. For example, QA route had a 40% KV hit which reduced token spend by about 30% on the sample data here.
[00:03:20] Jordan: Nice. Can that caching be shared across projects or across VPCs?
[00:03:25] Priya: Within a single deployment you can scope caches by route/tags. Cross-VPC is restricted for security — if you go Private (our VPC/on-prem deployment) you control whether caches are shared.
[00:03:36] Maya: Speaking of private — can you summarize the security posture? We need SOC 2, KMS support, and audit logs.
[00:03:44] Alex: Yes. We have SOC 2 Type II, SSO with SAML and OIDC, RBAC, and KMS integrations for key wrapping. We'll share the security pack after this call.
[00:03:55] Jordan: Is KMS per-customer? We need keys not accessible to Redwood ops team.
[00:04:01] Alex: For Private deployments you can provide your own KMS/HSM. For hosted we support customer-managed keys in supported clouds with dedicated key policies. We'll put the exact options in the doc.
[00:04:12] [00:04:20] Priya: Back to Console — here's the per-route cost breakdown chart. Notice the spike on July 4th sample window — that's because you had long-run batch jobs hitting the summarization route. Our Alerts engine could have flagged the cost per hour and applied a throttle or routing switch.
[00:04:36] Leo: Can alerts trigger automation? Eg, scale-down or route to cache-only mode?
[00:04:41] Priya: Alerts can trigger webhooks or internal runbooks. We also provide autoscaling policies that throttle burst capacity or switch routing priorities when a budget threshold is crossed. For your use-case we recommended: hard budget per route plus a soft p95 latency guard.
[00:04:55] [00:05:05] Jordan: How granular is billing export? We need to push cost attribution to our internal finance system and tag chargebacks by team.
[00:05:12] Alex: Exports are per-request with route tags, model id, tokens, cost, and latency. You can export CSVs or push to S3/BigQuery on a schedule.
[00:05:22] Maya: Is there any data sampling? We need full fidelity for chargeback.
[00:05:27] Priya: Full-fidelity exports are available; note there's retention settings and you can extend retention for analytics add-on.
[00:05:34] [00:05:50] Sam: Two interoperability questions — first, we have an internal inference proxy today. How invasive is Redwood integration?
[00:05:57] Priya: Integration is either via simple REST API calls to Redwood hosted endpoints or you can use our SDK. For Private you deploy the inference runtime behind your VPC and change routing rules to point to the private endpoints. Minimal code changes if you keep the same HTTP contract.
[00:06:10] Jordan: Second, model versioning — we want canary releases of model upgrades per route.
[00:06:15] Priya: Console supports rollouts: canary %, A/B, and automatic rollback when quality monitors detect regressions. Rollouts are per-route and can pin to model versions independent of the infra underneath.
[00:06:27] [00:06:40] Leo: On the dedicated capacity pricing you walked me through earlier — is burst capacity charged differently? Sometimes we need occasional heavy batches.
[00:06:48] Alex: Dedicated capacity has baseline commit and a burst pool. We bill committed units monthly, and burst usage is billed hourly at a discounted incremental rate. We'll share concrete examples tailored to IrisAI's traffic in the post-call pricing doc.
[00:07:05] Jordan: Can you do an example mapping for a single feature — say 'doc-summarize'? Show how cost flows into invoices.
[00:07:12] Priya: Sure. I switch the Console to 'Feature Flow' — select doc-summarize route — here you see tokens by phase (context load, summarization, post-processing), model used, and then a cost waterfall. The waterfall shows base model cost, added infra (if using dedicated GPUs), and network egress if cross-region.
[00:07:33] Maya: Network egress surprises us — our pipelines sometimes pull large external docs. Is there a way to show egress-level chargeback?
[00:07:40] Priya: Yes, egress shows up as a separate line item in the export and in the waterfall. You can tag those flows and exclude them from product-level chargebacks if you want to allocate differently.
[00:07:51] [00:08:10] Jordan: A quick technical — your runtime supports continuous batching, right? How are tokens grouped across concurrent requests?
[00:08:18] Priya: We do continuous batching with request-level affinity and KV cache preservation per session. Batches are workload-aware; the kernel selector picks optimized kernels for the dominant sequence lengths. In practice you get better throughput for many short requests.
[00:08:33] Leo: Do we need to change how we maintain session keys? We use a sticky session to keep KV cache local.
[00:08:38] Priya: Sticky session works fine; we also provide a redis-backed KV cache for multi-instance setups.
[00:08:44] [00:09:00] Sam: On the QA side you mentioned quality monitors — can those be scheduled to run on new model variants?
[00:09:06] Priya: Yes, Optimize can run eval suites on each candidate model during rollout and will raise an alert if a metric drops beyond a threshold you set.
[00:09:15] Jordan: Suppose we want to cap cost per feature at $X/day. Can Console enforce that?
[00:09:21] Alex: You can set budget policies per route that either throttle, raise alerts, or proactively route to a cheaper variant. Enforcement has two flavors: soft (alerts + throttles) and hard (reject or queue). For customer UX we usually recommend soft first.
[00:09:36] [00:09:50] Maya: The team is also worried about multi-tenant isolation. If we go hosted, how do you guarantee tenant separation?
[00:09:57] Alex: Hosted is logically isolated with strict tenant boundaries in the control plane and data paths. For strict isolation you can choose Dedicated or Private where hardware boundaries can be enforced.
[00:10:06] Jordan: Any SLA around latency? We're targeting p99 under 500ms for small queries.
[00:10:12] Priya: For Dedicated we provide latency SLAs (configurable by commit tier). Hosted has best-effort but we publish performance profiles per model and region. We'll include sample p99 numbers for your expected sequence lengths.
[00:10:26] [00:10:40] Alex: Ok, last section — let's sketch a pilot. Idea: two-week pilot with a trial tenant, run per-route benchmark, collect outputs for quality check, then evaluate economics. We'll run the baseline with your anonymized sample traffic.
[00:10:52] Jordan: Sounds good. For pilot success criteria: 1) cost per 1k tokens within our target, 2) no quality regressions for top 50 prompts, 3) SSO and logging validation.
[00:11:03] Priya: Great, we'll map those to concrete evaluation metrics and share a scoring doc.
[00:11:10] [00:11:30] Sam: One last small item — does your Console support custom tagging on a per-request basis? We need to surface user_id and session_id for internal telemetry.
[00:11:38] Priya: You can add metadata headers; we recommend hashing PII fields before sending. The Console will accept arbitrary tags and will let you pivot on them in analytics.
[00:11:48] Leo: PII hashing is important; also retention policies — can we auto-delete payloads older than X days?
[00:11:54] Alex: Yes, configurable retention and purge policies exist, and for Private you can enforce shorter retention centrally.
[00:12:06] [00:12:30] Jordan: A small nit — sometimes the product names in these demos get mixed up, can Redwood send a concise doc describing the deployment topologies and the cost math? That would help our finance team.
[00:12:40] Alex: Absolutely — I'll send a one-pager + a spreadsheet with worked examples.
[00:12:47] [cross-talk] Maya: Perfect, thanks.
[00:12:55] Priya: Wrapping up, quick recap — we'll run a per-route benchmark, share pricing and SOC2/KMS docs, and set up a trial tenant. Any other open items?
[00:13:04] Jordan: Nope, that's it from me.
[00:13:06] Sam: Good.
[00:13:08] Leo: All good.
[00:13:10] Alex: Great, thanks everyone. We'll follow up with calendar invites for the trial onboarding and the benchmark sync.
[00:13:17] [00:13:20] Priya: End of call notes: some transcribed words may have mis-recognitions — e.g., 'KV cash' in earlier internal note — we'll correct in attachments.
[00:13:30] [call ends]

Notes: transcription had a few mis-hearings (SAML -> "Sammy", KV cache -> "KV cash"). Jessie from finance requested a worked example of burst vs committed billing in dollars; Alex to include in pricing doc. The team expressed preference for a two-week pilot with SSO and sample traffic.
